items.title: Scattering data of the central model class: the scattering motion, the impact parameter, the asymptotic directions, the deflection conventions and the uniform-incident preparation
items.statement:
This item fixes the **scattering data** of the restricted model class of
[[post-cm05-central-model]] and the preparation conventions in which the
scattering statements of this page are phrased. All objects are model data;
nothing here is a measured value.

**(i) The scattering model.** A **central scattering model** is a model of
class (i) of [[post-cm05-central-model]] with $N=2$ labels, masses
$m_1,m_2>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), no external forces, and a
static central pair potential $u\in C^2(J_0)$
([[def-cm-scattering-data]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]])
whose collision-excluded interval satisfies $(0,\infty)\subseteq J_0$, so
that the only forbidden configuration is the collision $r=0$. Its **reduced
problem** is the one-label problem of class (ii) with reduced mass
$\mu:=m_1m_2/(m_1+m_2)$ ([[def-cm01-units]]: $[\mu]=\mathsf M$) and the same
potential, presented through the relative coordinate $r=x_1-x_2$; by
[[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]] the relative coordinate of every motion of
the model is a central-force trajectory for $(\mu,u)$ and every pair of an
affine centre-of-mass motion and a solution of the reduced equation on a
common interval reconstructs a motion of the model.

**(ii) Scattering motions and their data.** Let $r:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$
be a central-force trajectory for $(\mu,u)$ defined on all of $\mathbb R$
with values $|r(t)|\in J_0$ and with constant angular momentum
$j=\mu\,r\times r'=Je_3\ne0$ for $J>0$ and an oriented orthonormal triad
$(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ ([[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]],
[[thm-cm-central-force-angular-momentum-conservation]],
[[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]],
[[lem-cm-oriented-orthonormal-triads]]). Call $r$ a **scattering motion** of
the model when it satisfies the hypotheses under which the page's scattering
theorems establish the limits below. Its **energy** is the constant
$$E:=\tfrac12\mu\lVert r'\rVert_2^2+u(\lvert r\rvert)>0$$
of [[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]] (constant by
[[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]] clause 4), its **asymptotic
velocities** are the limits
$$v_-:=\lim_{t\to-\infty}r'(t),\qquad v_+:=\lim_{t\to+\infty}r'(t),$$
taken in the sense of [[def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity]]
(their existence under the hypotheses is a theorem, not a convention), and
its **scattering speed** is
$$v_\infty:=\lVert v_-\rVert_2=\lVert v_+\rVert_2=\sqrt{2E/\mu},$$
the equality being part of the scattering theorems. The **incoming branch**
is the trajectory restricted to times before its apsis; the **impact
parameter** is the perpendicular distance from the force centre of the line
through the incoming branch, defined by
$$b:=\frac{\lVert r(t)\times v_-\rVert_2}{\lVert v_-\rVert_2} \qquad(t\ \text{on the incoming branch}),$$
with $\times$ the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]] and the
Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]; the value is independent
of $t$ because $r\times r'=j/\mu$ is constant, and the scattering theorems
identify it with the geometric distance, giving $b=J/(\mu v_\infty)$. Its
dimension is $[b]=\ell$.

**(iii) Polar advance and deflection conventions.** Fix polar data
$(\rho,\theta)$ of the scattering motion in the triad, $r=\rho\,n(\theta)$,
$n(\varphi):=\cos\varphi\,e_1+\sin\varphi\,e_2$
([[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]]), and let $t_*$ be an apsis time,
$|r(t_*)|=\min_t|r(t)|$. The **polar advance of one half** is
$$\Delta:=\theta(+\infty)-\theta(t_*)=\theta(t_*)-\theta(-\infty),$$
defined by the limits asserted in the scattering theorems, and the
**polar advance of the motion** is $2\Delta$. The **scattering angle** is the
undirected angle between the asymptotic velocity directions,
$$\theta_{\mathrm{s}}:=\arccos\!\left(\frac{\langle v_-,v_+\rangle}{\lVert v_-\rVert_2\,\lVert v_+\rVert_2}\right)\in[0,\pi],$$
equivalently the angle between the incoming and outgoing asymptote lines;
the **signed velocity rotation** is the continuous rotation angle of
$r'(t)$, measured counterclockwise about $e_3$ relative to the incoming
direction, so that a positive value is a counterclockwise turn. The scattering
theorems give $\cos\theta_{\mathrm{s}}=\cos(\pi-2\Delta)$ and the signed
rotation $2\Delta-\pi$; in particular, when $0<\Delta<\pi/2$ the scattering
angle is
$$\theta_{\mathrm{s}}=\pi-2\Delta\in(0,\pi),$$
while for $\Delta\ge\pi/2$ the motion has wrapped past the backward direction
and $\theta_{\mathrm{s}}$ is the wrapped value $\arccos(\cos(\pi-2\Delta))$.
The **deflection map** of a scattering model is the partial map
$b\mapsto\theta_{\mathrm{s}}(b)$ carrying the impact parameter of each
scattering motion that satisfies the hypotheses to its scattering angle;
the scattering theorems of the page determine its values on the hypotheses
they state, and **deflection branches** of it are the $C^1$ branches of
[[def-cm-scattering-data]].

**(iv) The uniform-incident preparation (adopted model datum).** The
**uniform-incident preparation** of a central scattering model with cutoff
$b_{\max}>0$ and flux $\Phi>0$ is the following adopted model of a scattering
experiment for the reduced problem: independent incident reduced labels, each
with energy $E>0$, angular momentum $Je_3$ and impact-azimuth pair
distributed with density $b\,\mathrm db\,\mathrm d\varphi$ on
$(0,b_{\max})\times(0,2\pi)$ normalised to unit total mass, where the
**incident flux** $\Phi$ is the number of incident labels per unit area per
unit time and $[\Phi]=\ell^{-2}\tau^{-1}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]). Under this
preparation the model predicts the expected rate
$$\dot N(A)= \Phi\cdot\nu(A)$$
of incident labels whose impact-azimuth pair lies in $A$, where $\nu$ is the
incident flux measure of [[def-cm-scattering-data]]; the rate of scattered
labels into a solid-angle set is the flux times the pushforward of $\nu$ under
the deflection map, whose density on a branch is the cross-section density
introduced in this page's cross-section definition. This is a predicted model
quantity: it reports no
detection, and its comparison with data requires a separately specified
experiment, apparatus model and statistical analysis.

**(v) Reading conventions.** All angles and lengths above are data of the
**relative** problem, equivalently of the centre-of-mass frame of the
two-label model: the relative coordinate $r$ and the centre of mass $X$ are
those of clause (i) and [[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]]. The
individual labels move along $x_1=X+\frac{m_2}{M}r$ and
$x_2=X-\frac{m_1}{M}r$ with $M=m_1+m_2$
([[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]] clause 4), so their directions relative to
the centre of mass differ from $r$ by the mass factors and generally differ
from each other; an angle of the reduced problem is not, without further
computation, an angle of either label with respect to a laboratory frame.
"Target", "projectile" and "detector" are names for model components and
carry no empirical claim.

**(vi) Exclusions and status.** The class excludes velocity- or
time-dependent, non-central and non-potential forces; constraints and
reaction forces; collisions $r=0$; external forces; and models with more than
two labels, exactly as in [[post-cm05-central-model]] clause (v). The
preparation of clause (iv) is one adopted idealisation among many; the
scattering theorems state separately which potentials, energies and angular
momenta produce the data of clauses (ii)-(iii). The quantities $\mu$, $u$
(with any parameters it carries), $E$, $J$, $b$, $b_{\max}$, $\Phi$ are model
data; quantitative empirical use requires separately stated measured inputs
with uncertainties, and no statement of this page asserts that any physical
system is exactly a central scattering model or that any beam is exactly
uniform.

**Why the objects are defined.** The relative coordinate is a central-force
trajectory by the cited reduction theorem; the attached energy and angular
momentum are defined by [[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]] and are constant
on the trajectory by [[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]] clause 4 and
[[thm-cm-central-force-angular-momentum-conservation]]; the impact parameter
is $t$-independent because $r\times r'=j/\mu$ is constant; and the
preparation measure of clause (iv) is the measure $\nu$ of
[[def-cm-scattering-data]]. The arccosine of clause (iii) is defined because
the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality gives
$|\langle v_-,v_+\rangle|/(\lVert v_-\rVert_2\lVert v_+\rVert_2)\le1$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

**Mathematical status.** The vocabulary is attached to the adopted model
class of [[post-cm05-central-model]]; the existence of the limits, the
identities for $v_\infty$, $b$, $\Delta$ and $\theta_{\mathrm{s}}$, and the
form of the deflection map under explicit potential hypotheses are the
content of the mathematics and physics theorems of this page, not of this
definition.

items.physical_scope: The physical reading of the scattering data of the page's restricted model class: the two-label central model of the central-model postulate, its reduced problem, the scattering motion of the relative coordinate on all of R, the energy and angular momentum carried by the motion, the asymptotic velocities, the impact parameter as the perpendicular distance of the incoming branch, the polar advance and the deflection conventions, the adopted uniform-incident preparation and its flux and units, and the reading conventions (angles are relative-frame angles) together with the explicit exclusions and the status of the data as model data. The item fixes vocabulary and an adopted preparation model; it asserts no observation, no measured value, no law of nature and no counting of detected particles.

items.title: The differential and truncated total cross-sections of a deflection branch: densities, units, branch sums and the empirical qualifications of the uniform-incident reading
items.statement:
This item fixes the **cross-section** vocabulary of the central scattering
models of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] relative to the uniform-incident
preparation of that definition.

**(i) The differential cross-section of a branch.** Let a central scattering
model be given, let $\theta:(a_1,a_2)\to(0,\pi)$ be a **deflection branch**
in the sense of [[def-cm-scattering-data]] — an interval $(a_1,a_2)$ of
impact parameters with $\theta$ of class $C^1$ and $\theta'(b)\ne0$ — and
suppose the branch **records the deflection** of the model: for every
$b\in(a_1,a_2)$ the scattering motion of the model with impact parameter $b$,
energy $E$ and angular momentum $J$ has scattering angle
$\theta_{\mathrm{s}}=\theta(b)$. Write
$(a_1,a_2)\ni b\mapsto\theta\in(\theta_1,\theta_2)$ for this bijection and
$b(\theta):=\theta^{-1}(\theta)$ for its inverse
([[def-cm-scattering-data]]). The **differential cross-section of the
branch** is the function
$$\frac{\mathrm d\sigma}{\mathrm d\Omega}(\theta):=\frac{b(\theta)\,\bigl|b'(\theta)\bigr|}{\sin\theta} =\frac{b(\theta)}{\sin\theta\,\bigl|\theta'\bigl(b(\theta)\bigr)\bigr|}\qquad(\theta_1<\theta<\theta_2),$$
the cross-section density of [[def-cm-scattering-data]]. Its dimension is
$[\mathrm d\sigma/\mathrm d\Omega]=\ell^2$ (solid angle dimensionless in the
chosen convention, [[def-cm01-units]]), and one says "per steradian" for the
unit of solid angle.

**(ii) Branch sums.** If finitely many deflection branches of the same model
have pairwise disjoint image intervals $(\theta_1^{(j)},\theta_2^{(j)})$ that
do not overlap and each records the model's deflections on its interval, the
**differential cross-section of the model** on the union of the images is the
sum of the branch densities, and it is left undefined at angles belonging to
no branch image. No claim is made that the branch images cover $(0,\pi)$ or
that the branch functions are reverse images of a single function.

**(iii) Truncated total cross-sections.** For an angular window
$Y\subseteq(0,\pi)$ the **solid-angle measure** of the branch is
$$\sigma(Y):=\int_Y\frac{\mathrm d\sigma}{\mathrm d\Omega}(\theta)\,2\pi\sin\theta\,\mathrm d\theta,$$
an ordinary Riemann integral when $Y$ is a compact interval contained in
$(\theta_1,\theta_2)$ and, when $Y$ has an endpoint at $\theta_1$ or
$\theta_2$ where the integrand is unbounded, the improper integral at that
endpoint in the sense of [[def-improper-integral-at-a-finite-endpoint]]
(two-sided improper integrals are those of
[[def-mixed-improper-integral]], with no cancellation between the sides). For
Borel windows the integral is that of [[def-mixed-improper-integral]] applied
to the two one-ended pieces. The **ideal total cross-section** of the branch
is $\sigma_{\mathrm{tot}}:=\sigma\bigl((\theta_1,\theta_2)\bigr)$ when it
converges; when it diverges the model simply has no ideal total on that
branch, and every angular window with a positive inner cutoff defines a
finite **truncated total cross-section**. By
[[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]] the truncated integral over
$(\theta_1,\theta)$ is nondecreasing in $\theta$, so a truncation can only be
finite or diverge, and no value is assigned at a divergence.

**(iv) The uniform-incident reading.** Under the uniform-incident preparation
of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (iv) with cutoff $b_{\max}$ and flux
$\Phi$, the model predicts the expected rate of scattered labels into an
angular window $Y$ to be $\Phi\,\sigma(Y)$, where the window is the image of
the interval of impact parameters feeding it. This is a prediction of the
model under the adopted preparation. In particular:

- $\sigma(Y)$ is **not** a probability per incident label, **not** a count of
  detected events, and **not** a property of any apparatus;
- a comparison with data requires a separately specified experiment: an
  apparatus model, a detector with finite angular resolution and acceptance,
  a sampling model and uncertainties, and a statistical analysis, none of
  which is supplied by this page;
- for a branch whose ideal total diverges at a forward angle, only truncated
  windows are defined, and a finite measured rate constrains the model only
  jointly with the apparatus acceptance;
- finite samples fluctuate: an observed angular distribution can miss a
  branch's features with positive probability under ordinary sampling models,
  and agreement is evidence about the model-plus-apparatus assumptions, not a
  proof of the model.

**(v) Status and exclusions.** The branch hypothesis includes
$\theta'\ne0$: the definition excludes angles at which
$\theta'(b)=0$ (rainbow-type stationary deflections) and leaves them to
separate limiting measures. It also excludes, at the level of this page,
friction and tangential contact laws, attractive capture, screening,
radiation, relativistic and quantum modifications, and any identification of
the model parameters with measured electromagnetic quantities; those require
separate models or cross-framework items. The functions $\theta$, $b$ and the
data $E$, $J$, $u$, $b_{\max}$, $\Phi$ are model data
([[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (vi)).

**Why the objects are defined.** The inverse $b$ is $C^1$ with
$b'(\theta)=1/\theta'(b(\theta))$ because a $C^1$ function on an interval with
nowhere vanishing derivative is strictly monotone and has a differentiable
inverse ([[def-cm-scattering-data]]); $\sin\theta>0$ on $(0,\pi)$; hence the
denominators do not vanish and the density is finite at every interior point
of the branch image. The pushforward identity that justifies the reading
"density carried by the branch" is
[[thm-cm-differential-cross-section-density]], a theorem of this page's
mathematical suppliers.
items.strategy: A vocabulary item: the differential cross-section of a deflection branch as an area-pushforward density, branch sums, truncated total cross-sections via improper integrals, the uniform-incident rate reading and its empirical qualifications.
items.physical_scope: The page's cross-section vocabulary for the uniform-incident preparation: the differential cross-section as the area-pushforward density of a deflection branch of a central scattering model, its units, the branch-sum convention, the truncated total cross-section over an angular window with finite or singular endpoints, and the empirical qualifications of the uniform-incident reading (adopted preparation, model rates not detections, finite samples, detector acceptance, no ideal total for a forward-divergent branch). The item defines model quantities; it asserts no observation, no measured value and no counting of detected particles.

items.title: Finite-range central scattering in the model class: the scattering motion on all of time, the asymptotic velocities and impact parameter $b=J/\\sqrt{2\\mu E}$, the advance $\\Delta$ with deflection $\\pi-2\\Delta$, and the cross-section of a deflection branch
items.statement:
Adopt a central scattering model of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (i)
with masses $m_1,m_2>0$, reduced mass $\mu=m_1m_2/(m_1+m_2)$, static
central pair potential $u\in C^2((0,\infty))$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), and let $E>0$, $J>0$; write
$$V(r):=u(r)+\frac{J^2}{2\mu r^2}\qquad(r>0).$$
Suppose:

**(H1) finite range:** there is $R>0$ with $u(r)=0$ for every $r\ge R$;

**(H2) simple outer turning point:** there is $r_*>0$ with
$$V(r_*)=E,\qquad V'(r_*)<0,\qquad V(r)<E\quad(r>r_*).$$

Let $r:J_0\to\mathbb R^3$ be the relative coordinate of a motion of the model
on an interval $J_0$ with nonempty interior and with attached angular
momentum $j=\mu\,r\times r'=Je_3\ne0$ and attached energy $E$
([[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]],
[[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]]), and suppose
$|r(t)|\ge r_*$ for every $t\in J_0$ and $|r(t_*)|=r_*$ for some
$t_*\in J_0$. Then:

1. **(The scattering motion.)** $r$ extends uniquely to a central-force
   trajectory $\bar r:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ for $(\mu,u)$; the extension is
   the relative coordinate of a motion of the two-label model defined on all
   of $\mathbb R$, whose centre of mass is the affine extension of the
   original one. Along $\bar r$, $\rho:=|\bar r|$ satisfies $\rho\ge r_*$,
   $\rho(t)>r_*$ for $t\ne t_*$, and $\rho$ is strictly decreasing on
   $(-\infty,t_*]$ and strictly increasing on $[t_*,\infty)$; no collision
   occurs. Moreover the time quadrature
   $$\tau(r_0):=\int_{r_*}^{r_0}\frac{\mathrm ds}{\sqrt{(2/\mu)\bigl(E-V(s)\bigr)}}\qquad(r_0\ge r_*)$$
   is finite for every $r_0$ and satisfies $\rho(t_*\pm\tau(r_0))=r_0$.
2. **(Free asymptotes, speed and impact parameter.)** The limits
   $v_\pm=\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}\bar r'(t)$ exist and
   $$|v_+|=|v_-|=\sqrt{2E/\mu}=:v_\infty .$$
   For every $t_1\ge t_*$ with $\rho(t_1)\ge R$ the motion is exactly free
   from $t_1$ on, $\bar r(t)=\bar r(t_1)+(t-t_1)v_+$ for all $t\ge t_1$;
   symmetrically for the incoming branch with $v_-$. The perpendicular
   distance from the force centre of the incoming line and of the outgoing
   line is the same number
   $$b=\frac{J}{\mu v_\infty}=\frac{J}{\sqrt{2\mu E}},\qquad\text{so that}\qquad J=\mu b\,v_\infty .$$
3. **(Polar advance and deflection.)** Let $(\rho,\theta)$ be polar data of
   $r$ in an oriented orthonormal triad with $e_3=j/J$
   ([[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]]). Then
   $$\Delta:=\theta(+\infty)-\theta(t_*)=\theta(t_*)-\theta(-\infty) =\int_{r_*}^{\infty}\frac{J\,\mathrm dr}{r^2\sqrt{2\mu\,\bigl(E-V(r)\bigr)}}$$
   is finite and positive, and the asymptotic directions satisfy
   $$\frac{v_+}{|v_+|}=-R_{2\Delta}\Bigl(\frac{v_-}{|v_-|}\Bigr),\qquad \frac{\langle v_-,v_+\rangle}{|v_-|\,|v_+|}=\cos(\pi-2\Delta),$$
   where $R_\alpha$ is the rotation of the plane
   $\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2)$ by $\alpha$. The scattering angle of the
   motion is $\theta_{\mathrm s}=\arccos(\cos(\pi-2\Delta))$; if
   $0<\Delta<\pi/2$ then $\theta_{\mathrm s}=\pi-2\Delta\in(0,\pi)$ and the
   signed velocity rotation is $2\Delta-\pi$.
4. **(Cross-section of a deflection branch.)** Let
   $\theta:(a_1,a_2)\to(0,\pi)$ be a deflection branch of the model in the
   sense of [[def-cm15-cross-section]]: $\theta$ is $C^1$ with
   $\theta'(b)\ne0$, and for every $b\in(a_1,a_2)$ the scattering motion of
   the model with impact parameter $b$, energy $E$ and angular momentum
   $Je_3$ has scattering angle $\theta_{\mathrm s}(b)=\theta(b)$, with
   $0<\Delta(b)<\pi/2$. Then, for every continuous
   $2\pi$-periodic $g:(0,\pi)\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$,
   $$\int_{a_1}^{a_2}\!\!\int_0^{2\pi} g\bigl(\theta(b),\varphi\bigr)\;b\;\mathrm db\,\mathrm d\varphi =\int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2}\!\!\int_0^{2\pi} g(\theta,\varphi)\;b(\theta)\,\bigl|b'(\theta)\bigr|\;\mathrm d\theta\,\mathrm d\varphi,$$
   the outgoing angular measure of the branch has density
   $b(\theta)|b'(\theta)|$ with respect to $\mathrm d\theta\,\mathrm d\varphi$,
   and the differential cross-section of the branch is
   $$\frac{\mathrm d\sigma}{\mathrm d\Omega}(\theta) =\frac{b(\theta)\,\bigl|b'(\theta)\bigr|}{\sin\theta} =\frac{b(\theta)}{\sin\theta\,\bigl|\theta'(b(\theta))\bigr|}\qquad(\theta_1<\theta<\theta_2).$$
   Under the uniform-incident preparation of
   [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (iv) with cutoff
   $b_{\max}\in(a_1,a_2]$ and flux $\Phi$, the model predicts the expected
   scattered rate
   $$\dot N=\Phi\,\sigma\bigl((\theta(a_1),\theta(b_{\max}))\bigr),\qquad \sigma(Y)=\int_Y\frac{\mathrm d\sigma}{\mathrm d\Omega}(\theta)\,2\pi\sin\theta\,\mathrm d\theta,$$
   into the corresponding window of scattering angles.
5. **(Scope of the statement.)** The theorem asserts nothing about the
   deflection map outside the recorded branch: it neither asserts that
   $b\mapsto\theta_{\mathrm s}$ is decreasing, injective or free of
   stationary points, nor that the branch images cover $(0,\pi)$; and it
   treats finite-range potentials only. The collisions, long-range
   potentials, velocity-dependent forces and external forces are excluded by
   the model class of [[post-cm05-central-model]] and by (H1).
items.strategy: A conditional deduction: transfer the model data to the finite-range scattering theory of the mathematical suppliers, reconstruct the model motion from the affine centre of mass and the global trajectory, and read off the asymptotic velocities, impact parameter, polar advance, deflection relation and branch cross-section.
items.physical_scope: The scattering prediction of the restricted two-label central model class with a finite-range $C^2$ potential and a simple outer turning point: the relative motion lives on all of time with one apsis and two monotone branches; the asymptotic velocities exist with speed $\\sqrt{2E/\\mu}$; beyond the range the branches are exactly free and the incoming and outgoing lines have perpendicular distance $b=J/\\sqrt{2\\mu E}$; the half-angle advance is the stated quadrature and the asymptotic directions satisfy the deflection relation with angle $\\pi-2\\Delta$ when $0<\\Delta<\\pi/2$; and on a smooth deflection branch that records the model's deflections the outgoing angular measure has cross-section density $b|\\mathrm db/\\mathrm d\\theta|/\\sin\\theta$ and the expected uniform-incident rate is the flux times the truncated cross-section. The result is a conditional deduction inside the adopted model class; it uses the model data $E,J,u$ and no measured value, asserts no monotonicity or completeness of the deflection map, and reports no detection.

items.title: Repulsive Coulomb scattering in the model class: global non-colliding motion, the deflection map $\\theta=2\\arctan(\\kappa/(2Eb))$, the Rutherford density $(\\kappa/4E)^2\\csc^4(\\theta/2)$, finite angular cutoffs and the divergent ideal total
items.statement:
Adopt a central scattering model of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (i)
with masses $m_1,m_2>0$, reduced mass $\mu$, and the **repulsive Coulomb
potential**
$$u(r)=\frac{\kappa}{r}\qquad(r>0),\qquad \kappa>0,$$
where $\kappa$ is a model datum of the mechanical model
([[def-cm01-units]]: $[\kappa]=\mathsf M\ell^3\tau^{-2}$), so that
$$V(r)=\frac{\kappa}{r}+\frac{J^2}{2\mu r^2}\qquad(r>0).$$
Let the data satisfy $E>0$, $J>0$ and put
$$b:=\frac{J}{\sqrt{2\mu E}}>0,\qquad \alpha:=\frac{\kappa}{2Eb}>0.$$
Then:

1. **(Turning data.)** $V$ is strictly decreasing on $(0,\infty)$, with
   $V(r)\to+\infty$ as $r\downarrow0$ and $V(r)\to0$ as $r\to\infty$; the
   equation $V(r)=E$ has exactly one solution $r_*>0$, it is simple
   ($V'(r_*)<0$), one has $V(r)<E$ for every $r>r_*$ and $V(r)>E$ for every
   $0<r<r_*$, and $V=U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J$ is of class $C^2$ with no other
   crossing of the level $E$.
2. **(Global non-colliding scattering motion.)** Let $r:J_0\to\mathbb R^3$
   be the relative coordinate of a motion of the model with attached angular
   momentum $j=\mu\,r\times r'=Je_3$ and energy $E$, with $|r(t)|\ge r_*$ for
   every $t\in J_0$ and $|r(t_*)|=r_*$ for some $t_*\in J_0$. Then $r$
   extends uniquely to a central-force trajectory $\bar r:\mathbb R\to
   \mathbb R^3$ whose extension is the relative coordinate of a motion of
   the two-label model on all of $\mathbb R$; $\rho:=|\bar r|$ satisfies
   $\rho\ge r_*>0$ (no collision), $\rho(t)>r_*$ for $t\ne t_*$, and $\rho$
   is strictly decreasing on $(-\infty,t_*]$ and strictly increasing on
   $[t_*,\infty)$; the asymptotic velocities $v_\pm=\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}
   \bar r'(t)$ exist with
   $|v_+|=|v_-|=\sqrt{2E/\mu}=:v_\infty$, and the asymptotic perpendicular
   distance of each branch to its limiting direction equals
   $b=J/(\mu v_\infty)=J/\sqrt{2\mu E}$, so that $J=\mu b\,v_\infty$. Unlike
   the finite-range case, there is no radius beyond which the motion is
   exactly free: the limits above are asymptotic.
3. **(Deflection and its single branch.)** With polar data $(\rho,\theta)$ in
   a triad with $e_3=j/J$, the half-angle of the motion is
   $$\Delta=\frac{\pi}{2}-\arctan\frac{\kappa}{2Eb}\in\Bigl(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\Bigr),$$
   its scattering angle is
   $$\theta_{\mathrm s}=\pi-2\Delta=2\arctan\frac{\kappa}{2Eb}\in(0,\pi),$$
   and its signed velocity rotation is $2\Delta-\pi=-2\arctan(\kappa/(2Eb))$.
   The **deflection map**
   $$\theta_{\mathrm{def}}:(0,\infty)\to(0,\pi),\qquad \theta_{\mathrm{def}}(b):=2\arctan\frac{\kappa}{2Eb},$$
   is $C^1$ and strictly decreasing, hence a $C^1$ bijection with inverse
   $b(\theta)=\dfrac{\kappa}{2E}\cot\dfrac{\theta}{2}$; it is a single
   deflection branch of the model on $(0,\infty)$ with
   $\theta_{\mathrm{def}}'(b)\ne0$ everywhere and no wrapping
   ($0<\Delta<\pi/2$ for every $b>0$).
4. **(Cross-section, angular cutoffs and divergence.)** The differential
   cross-section of that branch is
   $$\frac{\mathrm d\sigma}{\mathrm d\Omega}(\theta)=\Bigl(\frac{\kappa}{4E}\Bigr)^2\csc^4\frac{\theta}{2}\qquad(0<\theta<\pi),$$
   finite and positive; for $0<\theta_1<\theta_2<\pi$ the truncated total
   cross-section over the angular band is the finite number
   $$\sigma\bigl((\theta_1,\theta_2)\bigr) =\pi\bigl(b(\theta_1)^2-b(\theta_2)^2\bigr),$$
   and by monotonicity the band $\theta\ge\theta_1$ has
   $\sigma\bigl((\theta_1,\pi)\bigr)=\pi b(\theta_1)^2 =\pi\bigl(\frac{\kappa}{2E}\bigr)^2\cot^2\frac{\theta_1}{2}$; whereas the
   truncated integral over $(0,\theta_0)$ diverges for every
   $\theta_0\in(0,\pi)$, so the **ideal total cross-section of the model
   does not exist**. Every positive angular cutoff therefore yields a finite
   truncated cross-section, and the model is predictive only jointly with an
   angular acceptance.
5. **(Status of the parameter and exclusions.)** The coupling $\kappa$ is a
   parameter of the mechanical model. This item does not identify it with
   $q_1q_2/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$ or with any electromagnetic quantity, states
   no measured value, and asserts no screening law for a medium of
   scatterers. Attractive Coulomb scattering (for which capture is possible
   for suitable data), inelastic, radiative, relativistic and quantum
   modifications are outside the adopted model and this statement.
items.strategy: A Coulomb specialisation: verify the turning-point hypotheses from the strict monotonicity of the effective potential, apply the Coulomb scattering theorem to the model motion, identify the deflection map and its inverse, and evaluate the band cross-sections and the divergence by the fundamental theorem.
items.physical_scope: The Coulomb specialisation of the page's finite-range scattering statement, as a model prediction: the repulsive $\\kappa/r$ potential has a unique simple outer turning point and every relative motion of the stated data extends to all of time without collision, with asymptotic velocities of speed $\\sqrt{2E/\\mu}$ and asymptotic impact distance $b=J/\\sqrt{2\\mu E}$; the deflection map is the $C^1$ decreasing bijection $2\\arctan(\\kappa/(2Eb))$ with a single branch, the differential cross-section is the Rutherford density $(\\kappa/4E)^2\\csc^4(\\theta/2)$, every angular band has the finite truncated cross-section $\\pi(b(\\theta_1)^2-b(\\theta_2)^2)$, and the ideal total cross-section diverges at forward angles. The parameter $\\kappa$ is a model datum of the mechanical model and is not identified with any electromagnetic quantity; the result reports no measurement, no screening law and no capture, radiation, relativistic or quantum modification.

items.title: Adopted impact and open-mass extensions of the force branch: the isolated reciprocal impulse model, the collinear restitution contact law and the open-body material accounting
items.statement:
Adopt, as this page's **impact and open-mass extensions** of the force
branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and [[post-cm02-interactions]],
the following three model extensions. Each is an adopted model, not a
consequence of the smooth-force postulates; each applies only where a
statement explicitly invokes it.

**(i) The isolated reciprocal impulse model.** A two-label force model with
masses $m_1,m_2>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), time window $I_0$,
configuration domain $Q$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]) and continuous
external-plus-pair force maps $F_1,F_2$ is **run in the isolated reciprocal
impulse model at $t_*\in I_0$** when there is a motion
$x=(x_1,x_2):I\to Q$ of the associated first-order system
([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]) such that:

1. $x_1,x_2$ are continuous on $I$ and twice continuously differentiable on
   each of $I\cap(-\infty,t_*)$ and $I\cap(t_*,\infty)$
   ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]],
   [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), and
   $m_ix_i''(t)=F_i(t,x(t),x'(t))$ for every $t\in I\setminus\{t_*\}$;
2. the one-sided limits
   $v_i^{\pm}:=\lim_{t\to t_*\pm}x_i'(t)$ exist in $\mathbb R^3$
   ([[def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity]]);
3. there is a vector $J\in\mathbb R^3$, the **impulse**, with
   $$m_1\bigl(v_1^+-v_1^-\bigr)=J,\qquad m_2\bigl(v_2^+-v_2^-\bigr)=-J .$$

The two equations of clause 3 are the **reciprocal finite-jump form** of the
isolated impulse: the two labels receive equal and opposite momentum changes.
The model places no bound on the force maps across $t_*$; its distributional
rendering by test-function pairings is proved in
[[thm-cm-impulse-restitution-and-energy-loss]]. The dimension of the impulse
is $[J]=\mathsf M\ell\tau^{-1}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]).

**(ii) The collinear restitution contact law.** A model run in the isolated
reciprocal impulse model at $t_*$ is **collinear** when there is a unit vector
$n\in\mathbb R^3$ (the **contact direction**) with $v_i^{\pm}\parallel n$ for
$i=1,2$ and $\langle v_2^--v_1^-,n\rangle<0$ (the labels approach along $n$).
For a collinear contact, adopt a **coefficient of restitution** $e\in[0,1]$ —
a dimensionless model datum of the pair and the contact — and the **restitution
law**
$$v_2^+-v_1^+=-e\,\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr).$$
For $e=1$ the contact is called **elastic**, for $e=0$ **perfectly inelastic**
and otherwise **semi-elastic**; the law is a constitutive assumption, not a
consequence of the impulse equations of clause (i), and $e$ is not derived
from the masses or the approach speed. The law is stated only for a single
collinear contact; simultaneous contacts, repeated contacts and tangential
(friction) impulses are outside the model.

**(iii) The open-body material accounting.** Adopt for a body whose mass,
velocity, external force and exchanged matter are described by maps
$m:I\to(0,\infty)$, $v:I\to\mathbb R^3$, $F:I\to\mathbb R^3$,
$r_{\mathrm{in}},r_{\mathrm{out}}:I\to[0,\infty)$ and
$w_{\mathrm{in}},w_{\mathrm{out}}:I\to\mathbb R^3$ (mass rates and *inertial*
velocities of the matter entering and leaving, measured in the same inertial
frame as $v$) the **material balance identities**
$$m'=r_{\mathrm{in}}-r_{\mathrm{out}},\qquad (mv)'=F+r_{\mathrm{in}}\,w_{\mathrm{in}}-r_{\mathrm{out}}\,w_{\mathrm{out}} .$$
They are the mathematical rendering of "gains $r_{\mathrm{in}}\,\mathrm dt$ of
matter with velocity $w_{\mathrm{in}}$, loses $r_{\mathrm{out}}\,\mathrm dt$
with velocity $w_{\mathrm{out}}$, and feels the external force $F$", and they
are adopted rather than derived from a closed-system law. Their product-rule
consequence $mv'=F+r_{\mathrm{in}}(w_{\mathrm{in}}-v)-r_{\mathrm{out}}(w_{\mathrm{out}}-v)$
is proved in [[thm-cm-variable-mass-momentum-balance]]; in particular the
closed-system law $(mv)'=F$ is recovered only when
$r_{\mathrm{in}}w_{\mathrm{in}}=r_{\mathrm{out}}w_{\mathrm{out}}$.
The model parameters $r_{\mathrm{in}},r_{\mathrm{out}},w_{\mathrm{in}},w_{\mathrm{out}}$
are model data with $[r_{\mathrm{in}}]=[r_{\mathrm{out}}]=\mathsf M\tau^{-1}$
and $[w_{\mathrm{in}}]=[w_{\mathrm{out}}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$.
items.strategy: An adopted model extension: the isolated reciprocal impulse with its finite momentum jump, the collinear restitution contact law with coefficient in [0,1], and the open-body material accounting with entering and leaving mass rates and inertial velocities, together with their status and exclusions.
items.physical_scope: Adoption of the page's impact and open-mass extensions of the framework's force branch: an isolated reciprocal impulse at one time (a finite momentum jump of opposite sign for the two labels, with the regular dynamics retained away from that time), a collinear restitution contact law with coefficient $0\\le e\\le1$ fixing only the relative velocity, and an open-body material accounting for matter entering and leaving a body at given rates with given inertial velocities. The item adopts model extensions and names their mathematical renderings; it derives nothing from the smooth-force postulates, asserts no law of nature, no measured value for $e$, the impulse or the mass rates, and excludes simultaneous contacts, friction, deformation modes and coefficients outside $[0,1]$.

items.title: Consequences of the adopted impact and open-mass models: continuity of total momentum, the smooth-force exclusion, the restitution solution with $\\Delta K=-\\frac{1-e^2}{2}\\mu\\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\\rVert_2^2$, and the open-body and rocket laws
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]),
inherited from the statement of
[[thm-cm-impulse-restitution-and-energy-loss]], whose distributional jump
lemma uses it; the algebraic clauses used here do not otherwise use choice.
Adopt the impact and open-mass extensions of [[post-cm15-impulse]], with
$m_1,m_2>0$, an interval $I$ with nonempty interior, $t_*\in I$, a motion
$x=(x_1,x_2):I\to Q$ run in the isolated reciprocal impulse model at $t_*$
with impulse $J$ and one-sided velocities $v_i^\pm$, and write
$$M:=m_1+m_2,\qquad \mu:=\frac{m_1m_2}{M},\qquad P(t):=m_1x_1'(t)+m_2x_2'(t).$$
Then:

1. **(Momentum continuity.)** The total momentum is continuous across the
   impact,
   $$P(t_*^+)=P(t_*^-),\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \sum_{i=1}^2 m_i\bigl(v_i^+-v_i^-\bigr)=0,$$
   and the impulse delivered to label $1$ is removed from label $2$:
   $J=m_1(v_1^+-v_1^-)=-m_2(v_2^+-v_2^-)$.
2. **(Smooth-force exclusion.)** Let $x$ be a motion of the smooth force
   branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and
   [[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]] on $I$ along which the force maps are
   continuous. Then the momentum curves $p_i=m_ix_i'$ are of class $C^1$ on
   $I$; in particular
   $$p_i(t_*^+)=p_i(t_*^-)\qquad(i=1,2),$$
   so $J=0$: no motion of that class carries a nonzero isolated impulse. The
   finite-jump model of [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (i) is therefore a
   genuine extension of the smooth-force branch, not one of its cases.
3. **(Collinear restitution solution.)** Suppose in addition that the
   contact is collinear with contact direction $n$ and coefficient of
   restitution $e\in[0,1]$ ([[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (ii)). Then
   $$J=\mu(1+e)\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr),$$
   $J$ is parallel to $n$, the centre-of-mass velocity
   $V:=M^{-1}(m_1v_1^-+m_2v_2^-)$ is unchanged across the impact, and the
   post-impact velocities are
   $$v_1^+=V+\frac{m_2}{M}\,e\,\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr),\qquad v_2^+=V-\frac{m_1}{M}\,e\,\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr).$$
4. **(Kinetic energy of the impact.)** The kinetic-energy change across the
   impact is
   $$\Delta K:=\frac{m_1\lVert v_1^+\rVert_2^2+m_2\lVert v_2^+\rVert_2^2}{2} -\frac{m_1\lVert v_1^-\rVert_2^2+m_2\lVert v_2^-\rVert_2^2}{2} =-\frac{1-e^2}{2}\,\mu\,\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2\le0,$$
   with equality if and only if $e=1$ or $v_2^-=v_1^-$. For $0\le e<1$ the
   contact model is dissipative: the total kinetic energy of the two labels
   is not conserved across the impact, and the deficit
   $\frac{1-e^2}{2}\mu\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2$ is a quantity of the
   adopted contact law. This item identifies it with no measured heat,
   temperature, sound or deformation observable.
5. **(Momentum balance alone does not determine the impact.)** In the
   collinear case with $d^-:=v_2^--v_1^-$ and $d_n:=\langle d^-,n\rangle<0$,
   the impulse equations of clause 1 alone leave the scalar impulse magnitude
   free: for every real $J_n$ with $J_n\le \mu d_n$ (so that the contact is
   separating or grazing) the velocities
   $$v_1^+=v_1^-+\frac{J_n}{m_1}n,\qquad v_2^+=v_2^--\frac{J_n}{m_2}n$$
   satisfy the reciprocal impulse equations with impulse $J=J_nn$ and
   preserve the total momentum, and their kinetic-energy change is
   $$\Delta K(J_n)=-J_n\,d_n+\frac{J_n^2}{2\mu},$$
   whose minimum over the admissible range is
   $\Delta K(\mu d_n)=-\frac{\mu}{2}d_n^2$ at the perfectly inelastic value
   $J_n=\mu d_n$ (that is, $e=0$). The value of
   $J_n$ is fixed only by the contact law of [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause
   (ii), which selects $J_n=\mu(1+e)d_n$; in particular momentum balance
   alone does not determine the post-impact velocities.
6. **(Open-body and rocket laws.)** Under [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause
   (iii), with $m:I\to(0,\infty)$, $v:I\to\mathbb R^3$,
   $F,r_{\mathrm{in}},r_{\mathrm{out}}:I\to\dots$ and
   $w_{\mathrm{in}},w_{\mathrm{out}}:I\to\mathbb R^3$ satisfying the material
   balance identities, one has on $I$
   $$m\,v'=F+r_{\mathrm{in}}\bigl(w_{\mathrm{in}}-v\bigr)-r_{\mathrm{out}}\bigl(w_{\mathrm{out}}-v\bigr).$$
   In particular: (a) if $r_{\mathrm{in}}=r_{\mathrm{out}}=0$ then
   $m\,v'=F$ and $(mv)'=F$; (b) if $r_{\mathrm{in}}=0$ and
   $r_{\mathrm{out}}=-m'>0$ (mass loss) then
   $$m\,v'=F+r_{\mathrm{out}}\bigl(v-w_{\mathrm{out}}\bigr)=F-m'\bigl(v-w_{\mathrm{out}}\bigr),$$
   so the **thrust** is $T:=r_{\mathrm{out}}(v-w_{\mathrm{out}})=-m'(v-w_{\mathrm{out}})$,
   and the closed-system law $(mv)'=F$ fails unless
   $w_{\mathrm{out}}=v$; (c) if $r_{\mathrm{out}}=0$ and $w_{\mathrm{in}}=0$
   then $m\,v'=F-r_{\mathrm{in}}v$, so capturing matter at rest in the
   inertial frame decelerates the body while $(mv)'=F$ still holds.
items.strategy: A conditional deduction from the adopted models: momentum continuity across the impulse, the smooth-force exclusion, the restitution velocities and kinetic-energy change, the underdetermination by momentum alone, and the open-body and rocket laws with their special cases.
items.physical_scope: The conditional consequences of the page's adopted impact and open-mass extensions: total momentum is continuous across an isolated reciprocal impulse with the impulse removed from the second label; a smooth-force motion with continuous force maps cannot carry a nonzero impulse, so the contact model is an extension rather than a smooth-force theorem; a collinear contact with coefficient of restitution $e\\in[0,1]$ has the stated post-impact velocities and kinetic-energy change, is dissipative for $e<1$, and its contact law is an independent assumption not derivable from momentum balance; and the open-body material accounting yields the derived law $mv'=F+r_{\\mathrm{in}}(w_{\\mathrm{in}}-v)-r_{\\mathrm{out}}(w_{\\mathrm{out}}-v)$ with the rocket thrust as the special case. The result is a conditional deduction from adopted model data; it asserts no measured value of $e$, the impulse or the mass rates, and identifies no observed dissipation mechanism.

items.title: The smooth open-flow model: moving-control-region mass and momentum balances, their material and fixed special cases, and the inlet/outlet decomposition reproducing the open-body and rocket laws
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), as used by the transport and divergence theorems.
**Adopt the smooth open-flow model** with the following model data
([[def-cm-continuum-motion]], [[def-cm-euclidean-spatial-calculus]],
[[post-cm01-worldlines]], [[def-cm01-units]]): a nonempty open interval $I$;
a material region $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ (bounded open with $C^1$ boundary);
a motion $\chi$ of $B$ on $I$ of class $C^2$ whose time slices are
diffeomorphisms with positive Jacobian onto their images; a density field
$\rho>0$ of class $C^1$ and a spatial velocity field $u$ (the velocity of
$\chi$); a stress field $\sigma$ of class $C^1$
([[def-cm-traction-and-stress]]); and a continuous body-force density $b$;
all fields defined on a neighbourhood of the swept region over a compact
subinterval $J_0$ with $\overline{J_0}\subseteq I$. Adopt as the model's
**material balances**: for every material subregion $B'\subseteq B$ (a
nonempty bounded open subset with $\overline{B'}\subseteq B$ whose images
$\chi_t(B')$ are bounded $C^1$ domains,
[[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]) and every
$t\in J_0$,

$$\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\int_{\chi_t(B')}\rho\,\mathrm dx=0,\qquad \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\int_{\chi_t(B')}\rho u\,\mathrm dx=\int_{\chi_t(B')}\rho b\,\mathrm dx+\int_{\partial\chi_t(B')}\sigma\nu\,\mathrm dS,$$

with $\nu$ the outward unit normal and the surface integral that of
[[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]. These two balance
laws are **adopted model assumptions** of this item, in the sense of the
open-body accounting of [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (iii); they are not
derived from the particle postulates. Then, for every second motion $\psi$ of
a material region $B'\subseteq B$ on $I$ (the **control motion**) with
control regions $C_t:=\psi_t(B')$ that are bounded $C^1$ domains for
$t\in J_0$, spatial velocity $w$, and outward unit normal $\nu$.
Require its closed sweep $\Sigma_C:=\{(t,x):t\in\overline{J_0},\ x\in\psi_t(\overline{B'})\}$ to lie in the common open field domain. Require also either that this sweep lie locally inside the current material region $\chi_t(B)$, where localization supplies the local mass and momentum equations, or that those same local equations $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0$ and $\rho D_tu=\rho b+g$ be explicitly adopted on a neighbourhood of the control sweep. The control motion need not coincide with $\chi$. Then:

1. **(Control-volume identities.)** For every $t\in J_0$,
   $$\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\int_{C_t}\rho\,\mathrm dx =-\int_{\partial C_t}\rho\,(u-w)\cdot\nu\,\mathrm dS, \tag{CV1}$$
   and componentwise
   $$\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\int_{C_t}\rho u_i\,\mathrm dx =\int_{C_t}\rho b_i\,\mathrm dx+\Bigl(\int_{\partial C_t}\sigma\nu\,\mathrm dS\Bigr)_i -\int_{\partial C_t}\rho u_i\,(u-w)\cdot\nu\,\mathrm dS\qquad(i=1,2,3). \tag{CV2}$$
2. **(Material and fixed special cases.)** If $\psi=\chi$ (the control region
   is material, $w=u$ on the boundary), the flux terms vanish and (CV1),
   (CV2) reduce to the adopted material balances; if $\psi$ is the constant
   motion ($w=0$, $C_t=C$ fixed), then
   $$m_C'=-\int_{\partial C}\rho\,u\cdot\nu\,\mathrm dS,\qquad P_C'=\int_C\rho b\,\mathrm dx+\int_{\partial C}\sigma\nu\,\mathrm dS-\int_{\partial C}\rho u\,(u\cdot\nu)\,\mathrm dS$$
   with $m_C:=\int_C\rho$, $P_C:=\int_C\rho u$; the last term is the momentum
   flux through the fixed boundary, and the relation is the fixed-region
   steady-flow balance of the engineering treatment when the fields are
   steady and the region fixed.
3. **(Inlet/outlet decomposition and the open-body law.)** Suppose that for
   every $t\in J_0$ the boundary decomposes into finitely many $C^1$ pieces,
   among which $\Sigma_{\mathrm{in},t}$ (where $(u-w)\cdot\nu<0$),
   $\Sigma_{\mathrm{out},t}$ (where $(u-w)\cdot\nu>0$) and the zero-flux rest,
   and put
   $$r_{\mathrm{in}}:=-\int_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{in},t}}\rho\,(u-w)\cdot\nu\,\mathrm dS\ge0,\qquad r_{\mathrm{out}}:=\int_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{out},t}}\rho\,(u-w)\cdot\nu\,\mathrm dS\ge0,$$
   $$w_{\mathrm{in}}:=\frac{1}{r_{\mathrm{in}}}\int_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{in},t}}\rho u\,\bigl(-(u-w)\cdot\nu\bigr)\mathrm dS,\qquad w_{\mathrm{out}}:=\frac{1}{r_{\mathrm{out}}}\int_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{out},t}}\rho u\,\bigl((u-w)\cdot\nu\bigr)\mathrm dS$$
   (the flux averages are used only where the corresponding rate is
   positive), and write
   $$m:=\int_{C_t}\rho\,\mathrm dx>0,\qquad P:=\int_{C_t}\rho u\,\mathrm dx,\qquad F_{\mathrm{ext}}:=\int_{C_t}\rho b\,\mathrm dx+\int_{\partial C_t}\sigma\nu\,\mathrm dS .$$
   Then the control-volume identities read
   $$m'=r_{\mathrm{in}}-r_{\mathrm{out}},\qquad P'=F_{\mathrm{ext}}+r_{\mathrm{in}}\,w_{\mathrm{in}}-r_{\mathrm{out}}\,w_{\mathrm{out}},$$
   and the lumped body with mass $m$ and velocity $v:=P/m$ satisfies
   $$m\,v'=F_{\mathrm{ext}}+r_{\mathrm{in}}\bigl(w_{\mathrm{in}}-v\bigr)-r_{\mathrm{out}}\bigl(w_{\mathrm{out}}-v\bigr),$$
   the derived law of [[thm-cm-variable-mass-momentum-balance]]. In
   particular, a body that only loses mass ($r_{\mathrm{in}}=0$,
   $r_{\mathrm{out}}=-m'$) has thrust
   $r_{\mathrm{out}}(v-w_{\mathrm{out}})=-m'(v-w_{\mathrm{out}})$, and a body
   whose boundary moves with the material ($w=u$; no flux) has
   $m'=0$ and $P'=F_{\mathrm{ext}}$.
4. **(Status.)** The balances displayed before clause 1 are adopted component
   models of the open flow, exactly as clause (iii) of
   [[post-cm15-impulse]] adopts the lumped accounting; this item proves only
   the two stated deductions (localization followed by the control-volume
   identities, and the inlet/outlet reading). It asserts no constitutive law
   for $\rho$ or $\sigma$, no boundary condition, no incompressibility, no
   smoothness beyond the stated one, and no empirical claim; the fields,
   the control motion and the region are model data.
items.strategy: A conditional deduction: localize the adopted material balances to the field equations, apply the control-volume theorem to an arbitrary control motion, and decompose the boundary flux into inlet and outlet rates and flux-averaged inertial velocities, reproducing the lumped open-body law.
items.physical_scope: The moving-control-region bookkeeping of the adopted smooth open-flow model: under the adopted material mass and momentum balances for every material subregion, a non-material control region has the stated mass and momentum rates with boundary speed $w$, the material and fixed special cases follow, and under an inlet/outlet split of the boundary the flux terms become the entering and leaving mass rates with flux-averaged inertial velocities, so that the lumped open body obeys the material accounting and rocket law adopted in the impulse postulate. The balances are adopted hypotheses of this item, not derivations from particle mechanics; the result asserts no constitutive law, no boundary condition, no measured value and no observational claim.

title: Scattering and impulse model boundaries — Examples

items.title: Elastic reflection from a fixed sphere: the branch $b=a\\cos(\\theta/2)$, the uniform density $a^2/4$ and the total $\\pi a^2$ of a contact model
items.statement:
**Declared model.** Fix a length $a>0$ (the sphere radius) and a reduced mass
$\mu>0$, and consider a label of mass $\mu$ moving in the plane in the
presence of a fixed impenetrable sphere of radius $a$ centred at the origin.
The adopted **elastic reflection rule** at a contact point with outward unit
normal $n$ is
$$v^+=v^--2\langle v^-,n\rangle n,$$
that is, the normal component of the velocity reverses and the tangential
component is unchanged; this is the infinite-mass, $e=1$ member of the
contact family of [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (ii) (the second label is
frozen and its mass is not treated as finite), and it is the contact rule of
the impenetrable-sphere model. Let the label approach from infinity along a
straight line with speed $v_\infty>0$, impact parameter $b\in(0,a)$ and
velocity direction $\hat u$, and let $P$ be the contact point, so that
$|OP|=a$ and the inward unit normal $-n=-P/a$ makes the angle
$$\alpha:=\arcsin\frac{b}{a}\in\Bigl(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\Bigr)$$
with $\hat u$; equivalently $b=a\sin\alpha$ is the perpendicular distance of
the incoming line from the centre.

**Assertion to check.** The motion is a single reflection with deflection
$$\theta(b)=\pi-2\alpha=\pi-2\arcsin\frac{b}{a}\in(0,\pi),$$
so the branch is $b(\theta)=a\cos(\theta/2)$ on $0<\theta<\pi$, the
differential cross-section is the constant $a^2/4$, and the truncated total
cross-section over the whole branch is $\pi a^2$.
items.strategy: A contact-model check: geometry of the reflection at a fixed sphere, the branch b = a cos(theta/2), the constant density a^2/4 and the total pi a^2, with the model-boundary warning.
items.physical_scope: A declared contact model of a reduced label of mass $\\mu$ reflecting elastically from a fixed impenetrable sphere of radius $a$: the reflection rule reverses the normal velocity component and preserves the tangential component, so that speed and angular momentum are conserved across the contact; the example computes the branch $b=a\\cos(\\theta/2)$, the uniformly constant cross-section density $a^2/4$ and the truncated total $\\pi a^2$, and records that this is a contact (impulse) model outside the $C^2$ finite-range hypothesis of the central-scattering theorem, so its finite total does not contradict the Coulomb forward divergence. The data are declared model data; the example reports no observation and no measured value.

items.title: A declared-data Rutherford check: $\\alpha=1$, $\\theta=\\pi/2$, $(\\mathrm d\\sigma/\\mathrm d\\Omega)=4\\times10^{-24}\\,\\mathrm{m^2}$, the band values $\\pi b(\\theta_1)^2$ and the growth of the truncated total as $\\theta_1\\downarrow0$
items.statement:
**Declared model data.** For a central scattering model of
[[pthm-cm15-rutherford-model]] declare the repulsive Coulomb coupling and
the reduced data
$$\mu=2\times10^{-26}\ \mathrm{kg},\qquad E=10^{-18}\ \mathrm{J},\qquad J=4\times10^{-34}\ \mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}},\qquad \kappa=4\times10^{-30}\ \mathrm{J\,m},$$
all read as *model data*, not as measured values of any physical pair.
Abbreviate $\kappa_4:=\kappa/(4E)=10^{-12}\ \mathrm{m}$ and
$\kappa_2:=\kappa/(2E)=2\times10^{-12}\ \mathrm{m}$.

**Assertions to check.** The model quantities of
[[pthm-cm15-rutherford-model]] take the values
$$v_\infty=10^4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}},\qquad b=2\times10^{-12}\ \mathrm{m},\qquad \alpha:=\frac{\kappa}{2Eb}=1,\qquad \theta=\frac{\pi}{2},$$
the branch density at $\theta=\pi/2$ is
$(\mathrm d\sigma/\mathrm d\Omega)(\pi/2)=\kappa_4^2\csc^4(\pi/4)=4\times10^{-24}\ \mathrm{m^2}$,
the angular band $(\theta_1,\theta_2)$ carries the truncated total
$\sigma=\pi\bigl(b(\theta_1)^2-b(\theta_2)^2\bigr)$ with
$b(\theta)=\kappa_2\cot(\theta/2)$, and as $\theta_1\downarrow0$ the band
value $\pi b(\theta_1)^2$ grows like
$(16\pi\times10^{-24}\ \mathrm{m^2})/\theta_1^2$, so no ideal total is
assigned.
items.strategy: A declared-data numeric check in SI units: v_inf, b, alpha=1, theta=pi/2, the density 4e-24 m^2, finite band values and the small-angle growth of the truncated total.
items.physical_scope: A numerical check of the repulsive-Coulomb model prediction on declared model data in SI units: reduced mass $2\\times10^{-26}\\,\\mathrm{kg}$, energy $10^{-18}\\,\\mathrm{J}$, angular momentum $4\\times10^{-34}\\,\\mathrm{kg\\,m^2\\,s^{-1}}$ and coupling $\\kappa=4\\times10^{-30}\\,\\mathrm{J\\,m}$ give $v_\\infty=10^4\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$, $b=2\\times10^{-12}\\,\\mathrm{m}$, $\\alpha=1$, scattering angle $\\pi/2$ and density $4\\times10^{-24}\\,\\mathrm{m^2}$; the angular band values $\\pi(b(\\theta_1)^2-b(\\theta_2)^2)$ and the small-angle growth $\\approx(16\\pi\\times10^{-24}\\,\\mathrm{m^2})/\\theta_1^2$ are checked. All numbers are declared model data fed into the model formulas; the example asserts no measurement, no uncertainty budget and no comparison with any experiment.

items.title: Smooth finite-range free scattering refutes global strict decrease; as a separate contact comparison, an attractive refracting shell with index $3/2$ has $\theta(b)=2(\arcsin(b/a)-\arcsin(2b/(3a)))$ strictly increasing, with a jump down to $0$ at grazing incidence
items.statement:
**False statement.** *Let a conservative central scattering model with a
finite-range interaction, positive energy and nonzero angular momentum have
a unique scattering angle for every impact parameter. Then the scattering
angle is a strictly decreasing function of the impact parameter.*

The smooth finite-range witness below refutes this claim within the exact
central-scattering class of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]]: the zero potential
has deflection $0$ at every positive impact parameter. More generally,
beyond the range of any finite-range potential the scattering trajectories
are free, so a globally defined deflection map has a constant tail. The
separate adopted refracting-shell comparison retains its increasing branch;
that contact rule is outside the smooth $C^2$ class and is not used as the
witness for the stated claim. [[pthm-cm15-central-scattering]] clause 5 makes
no global monotonicity assertion, and [[def-cm15-cross-section]] uses
specified deflection branches instead of inverting a global decreasing map.
items.strategy: A refutation by witness: the attractive refracting-shell rule gives an explicitly increasing deflection on (0,a) with a jump to zero at grazing incidence, so the unqualified monotonicity claim fails.
items.physical_scope: The smooth finite-range model has zero deflection for every impact parameter beyond its range, so any globally defined deflection map is constant on this tail and cannot be strictly decreasing. The zero potential is a genuine smooth witness with unique deflection for every positive impact parameter. As a separate model comparison, the adopted attractive refracting shell of index 3/2 retains its strictly increasing deflection on 0<b<a and its declared grazing jump to zero; it is outside the smooth central-scattering class. All computations concern declared model data and report no observations.

items.title: A declared-data impact check: $m_1=2\\,\\mathrm{kg}$, $m_2=6\\,\\mathrm{kg}$, $v_1^-=3\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$, $v_2^-=-1\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$, with elastic, semi-elastic and sticking outcomes
items.statement:
**Declared model data.** Adopt a collinear impact of two labels of the
contact model of [[post-cm15-impulse]] clauses (i)-(ii) along the contact
direction $n$, with masses and incoming velocities
$$m_1=2\ \mathrm{kg},\qquad m_2=6\ \mathrm{kg},\qquad v_1^-=3\,n\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}},\qquad v_2^-=-1\,n\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}} .$$
Thus $M=8\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\mu=\frac{2\cdot6}{8}=\frac32\ \mathrm{kg}$,
$V=\frac{2\cdot3+6\cdot(-1)}{8}=0$, and the relative velocity is
$d^-:=v_2^--v_1^-=-4\,n\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

**Assertions to check.** For $e=1$ (elastic): $v_1^+=-3n$,
$v_2^+=+1n$, $\Delta K=0$. For $e=\frac12$: $v_1^+=-\frac32n$,
$v_2^+=+\frac12n$, impulse $J=-9n\ \mathrm{N\,s}$,
$\Delta K=-9\ \mathrm{J}$. For $e=0$ (sticking): $v_1^+=v_2^+=0$,
$\Delta K=-12\ \mathrm{J}$. In every case the total momentum $P=0$ is
continuous across the impact, as [[pthm-cm15-impact-balance]] clause 1
requires, and the energy changes are those of its clause 4.
items.strategy: A declared-data impact check: elastic, semi-elastic and sticking outcomes for one data set, verifying momentum continuity, the impulse, the velocities and the energy changes.
items.physical_scope: A declared-data check of the adopted collinear impact model: masses $2$ and $6\\,\\mathrm{kg}$ with one-dimensional velocities $3$ and $-1\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$ along the contact direction, for coefficients of restitution $e=1,\\frac12,0$; the example verifies total momentum continuity, the impulse $J=-9\\,\\mathrm{N\\,s}$ at $e=\\frac12$, the post-impact velocities, and the kinetic-energy changes $0,-9,-12\\,\\mathrm{J}$, all in SI units. Every number is declared model data substituted into the model formulas; the example reports no measurement and no empirical comparison.

items.title: A coefficient of restitution above $1$ manufactures kinetic energy: $e=2$ on $m_1=m_2=1\\,\\mathrm{kg}$ with velocities $\\pm1\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$ raises the kinetic energy by $3\\,\\mathrm{J}$ while the configuration is unchanged
items.statement:
**False statement.** *In the collinear isolated-impact model of
[[post-cm15-impulse]] clauses (i)-(ii) for two fixed masses, launched
through a static central pair potential (so that away from the impact the
total mechanical energy $K+U$ with $U(x)=u(\lvert x_1-x_2\rvert)$ is
constant along the motion), every real value of the coefficient of
restitution $e$ yields a contact law under which the total mechanical energy
is conserved across the isolated impact.*

[[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (ii) restricts $e$ to $[0,1]$, and
[[pthm-cm15-impact-balance]] clause 4 computes the energy change of the
restricted law. The witness below shows that the restriction is not
decorative: an admissible-looking contact law with $e>1$ is incompatible
with the energy account, because the impact instantaneously changes only the
velocities while the positions — hence the potential energy — are
continuous.
items.strategy: A refutation by witness: with e=2 the contact law raises the kinetic energy by 3 J while the configuration is unchanged, so e>1 is incompatible with the conservative energy account.
items.physical_scope: A refutation of the claim that every real coefficient of restitution is admissible in the adopted isolated-impact model: with the collinear restitution law and $e=2$ on declared data, the kinetic energy rises by $3\\,\\mathrm{J}$ across an impact while the configuration is instantaneously unchanged, so the total mechanical energy of a conservative two-label model is not conserved; values $e>1$ therefore signal an omitted internal energy reservoir and are excluded from the conservative contact model of this page, which restricts $e$ to $[0,1]$. The witness uses declared model data and asserts no measurement.

items.title: Reciprocal impulses do not determine a collinear impact: the same incoming data admit the sticking outcome $v^+=0$ and the elastic outcome $(v_1^+,v_2^+)=(-3,1)\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$ with different impulses and energies
items.statement:
**False statement.** *In the collinear isolated-impact model of
[[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (i), the reciprocal impulse equations
$m_1(v_1^+-v_1^-)=J$ and $m_2(v_2^+-v_2^-)=-J$, with the impulse $J$
determined by momentum balance of the two labels, fix the post-impact
velocities for given incoming data; no additional contact law is needed.*

[[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (ii) adopts the restitution law as an
*independent* contact assumption, and [[pthm-cm15-impact-balance]] clause 5
records that the impulse equations leave the scalar impulse magnitude free.
The witness exhibits two admissible outcomes for one data set.
items.strategy: A refutation by witness: two admissible outcomes with different impulses satisfy the same reciprocal impulse equations, so an independent contact law is required.
items.physical_scope: A refutation of the claim that the reciprocal impulse equations alone determine a collinear impact: with masses $2$ and $6\\,\\mathrm{kg}$ and incoming velocities $3$ and $-1\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$, both the sticking outcome and the elastic outcome satisfy the equal-and-opposite momentum jumps with impulses $-6\\,\\mathrm{N\\,s}$ and $-12\\,\\mathrm{N\\,s}$ respectively and total momentum $0$, while velocities and kinetic-energy changes differ. Hence the contact law fixing the impulse (or the coefficient of restitution) is an independent model datum. The witness uses declared model data and asserts no measurement, no determination of any real coefficient and no observation.

items.title: A declared rocket check: mass $3-t\\,\\mathrm{kg}$ and constant exhaust speed $2\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$ relative to the body give $v(t)=2\\ln(3/(3-t))\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$ and show that $(mv)'=F$ fails
items.statement:
**Declared model data.** Adopt the open-body material accounting of
[[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (iii) with, on the interval $I=(0,\frac52)$,
$$m(t):=3-t\ \mathrm{kg},\qquad F\equiv0,\qquad r_{\mathrm{in}}\equiv0,\qquad r_{\mathrm{out}}\equiv1\ \mathrm{kg\,s^{-1}},\qquad w_{\mathrm{out}}(t):=v(t)-u_e\,n,$$
with a fixed unit vector $n$, $u_e:=2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and initial
velocity $v(0)=0$. The ejecta therefore leave with the body's velocity
reduced by the constant exhaust speed $u_e$ along $n$.

**Assertions to check.** The balance identities hold with
$$v(t)=u_e\ln\frac{m(0)}{m(t)}=2\ln\frac{3}{3-t}\ n\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\qquad(0\le t<2),$$
the thrust is $r_{\mathrm{out}}u_e=2\ \mathrm{N}$ along $n$, and the naive
closed-system law $(mv)'=F$ fails: it would force $v\equiv0$ on $I$.
items.strategy: A declared-data check of the open-body law: linear mass loss with constant relative exhaust speed gives the Tsiolkovsky velocity and shows that the closed-system law fails.
items.physical_scope: A declared-data check of the open-body material accounting: a body of initial mass $3\\,\\mathrm{kg}$ losing mass at $1\\,\\mathrm{kg\\,s^{-1}}$ with no external force and ejecta of constant speed $2\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$ relative to the body has velocity $v(t)=2\\ln(3/(3-t))\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$ from rest, satisfies the material balance identities, and violates the naive closed-system law $(mv)'=F$; the example verifies the identities, the thrust $2\\,\\mathrm{N}$ and the failure of the naive law on declared model data. It reports no measurement, no engine data and no empirical comparison.

items.title: A declared smooth open flow: the uniform expansion $\\rho=\\rho_0e^{-3\\alpha t}$, $u=\\alpha x$ satisfies the control-volume identities on fixed and material regions, and an ideal elbow illustrates the inlet/outlet decomposition
items.statement:
**(i) Declared uniform expansion.** Fix constants $\rho_0>0$ and
$\alpha\ne0$, and on an open interval $I\ni0$ declare the fields
$$\rho(t)=\rho_0e^{-3\alpha t},\qquad u(t,x)=\alpha x,\qquad \sigma(t,x)=-p(t,x)\,\mathrm{Id},\qquad p(t,x)=p_0-\frac{\rho(t)\alpha^2}{2}\lvert x\rvert^2,\qquad b\equiv0,$$
on $x$ in a neighbourhood of the closed ball $\overline{B_R}$ and of the
swept family $R(t)=R_0e^{\alpha t}$ with $R_0>0$. This is a declared exact
solution of the adopted balances of [[pthm-cm15-control-volume-balance]]
(its density is spatially uniform, its velocity is the conformal field
$\alpha x$, and the pressure is quadratic).

**(ii) Declared ideal elbow.** Declare a steady incompressible ideal flow in a
device that turns the stream by $90^\circ$: density $\rho=1000\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$,
inlet area $A_{\mathrm{in}}=10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^2}$, inlet speed
$v_{\mathrm{in}}=4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ along $\hat x$, outlet area
$A_{\mathrm{out}}=5\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{m^2}$, outlet velocity along
$\hat y$, zero body force, and the idealisation that the pressure part of the
boundary force is negligible compared with the momentum-flux part (equal
ambient pressure at inlet and outlet, inviscid walls). Adopt the local mass
and momentum equations of the smooth open-flow model on a neighbourhood
of the closed fixed elbow control region, within the common field domain.
items.strategy: Two declared checks: the exact uniform-expansion field satisfies the control-volume identities on fixed and material balls, and the ideal elbow illustrates the inlet/outlet decomposition with the dynamic force.
items.physical_scope: Two declared checks of the smooth open-flow bookkeeping: (i) the exact uniform-expansion model $\\rho(t)=\\rho_0e^{-3\\alpha t}$, $u(t,x)=\\alpha x$, $p=p_0-\\rho\\alpha^2\\lvert x\\rvert^2/2$, whose fields satisfy the adopted local balances and whose fixed-ball and material-ball control regions satisfy the mass and momentum rates of the moving-control-region theorem; (ii) an idealised steady elbow with declared inlet/outlet data, where the inlet/outlet split gives the mass flux $2/5\\,\\mathrm{kg\\,s^{-1}}$ and the dynamic force $\\lvert\\dot m(v_{\\mathrm{out}}-v_{\\mathrm{in}})\\rvert=8\\sqrt5/5\\,\\mathrm{N}$ once the pressure part is declared negligible. Both are conditional computations on declared fields; the example assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice $\\mathrm{AC}_\\omega$ inherited from the transport and divergence theorems that the cited control-volume statements use, and it reports no measurement and no solution of a boundary-value problem.
